c10_station.when: Friday, November 9, an hour before sunrise

chapter.title: Good Morning, Bellwether
chapter.goal: Steve wants to turn the fleet away.

c10_station.objective: Take back the microphone. Patch the show into the tower. Get the relay running.
notes: playlist keeps one board stage; AutoRick’s wrong-answer line is the board’s wrong_text.
route is a recall puzzle: the c8_rig.source finding records Birch, Elm and Ash.
relay uses the club operators planted in c5_shack: Gull (the operator voice), Marsh (out past Sentinel Point) and Cedar. Only stage 1 remains.
context: steve|One hour. The rig was in pieces, and all over town the copies were forgetting.
steve|Then I remembered Halcyon’s tower. Every ninth night for a year it had talked to the ship, alone.
intro: stephen|The rig is in pieces. We need another way onto their antenna.
steve|We don’t need the rig. KBWR’s tower already talks to the ship.

playlist.title: The radio host’s log
playlist.goal: Get the live microphone back from AutoRick.
playlist.background: AutoRick won’t give up the microphone. Its log from the last outage shows three slips used at 06:01, 06:03 and 06:05, but the slips have lost their headings: station ident, traffic report and news bulletin. Only the bulletin hands the air to a person.
lead: steve|Rick keeps a log of everything. Including the last time a human got the microphone.
steve|Three slips. My station ident, a traffic report and a news bulletin.
steve|The ident never stops the music. Traffic waits until the song ends. A bulletin puts a person on the air.
playlist.prompt: Which slip was used at each time?

board.instruction: Match each time in the log to the slip that was used.
evidence: At 06:01 the song kept playing, and the latch clicked the way it does for Steve’s station ident.
At 06:03 a traffic report waited in line until the song ended.
At 06:05 the song stopped, and a person spoke on the air right away.
Only the news bulletin slip has a line for the duty host to sign.

stages.prompt: Which slip was used at each time?

board.wrong_text: Great choice! Here is the traffic for yesterday.

hints: Read the log in time order. What happened to the song each time?
The ident never stops the music. Traffic waits for the song. Only one slip puts a person on the air.
At 06:05 a person spoke. Which slip has a line for the duty host to sign?
lines: c10_station.playlist.01
c10_station.playlist.02
playlist.finding: steve|06:01 was the ident, 06:03 the traffic and 06:05 the bulletin, the one that hands the air to a human. I signed the bulletin as duty host, and KBWR was mine again.

route.title: Tower patch panel
route.goal: Patch a live performance into the tower, on a return the fleet will trust.
route.background: The KBWR tower already talks to the ship. Wen has wired the jacks the way she did at the rig, with the same names. At the rig, Birch was Wen’s fixed tester, Ash was Shaw’s rehearsal loop, and Elm followed Shaw’s hand, live. The fleet trusts only what its own ship measures.
lead: wen|Same labels as the rig. You remember which is which, I hope.
steve|Birch was your fixed tester. Ash was the old rehearsal loop. Elm followed Shaw’s hand.
wen|Returns: A is the booth echo, B is a shore camera, and C is measured aboard their ship.
route.prompt: Which jack is the live source, and which return will the fleet accept?
route.instruction: Pick the jack that follows a live hand, and the return the fleet will believe. The fleet trusts only what its own ship measures.

rows.label: Which jack carries the live show?
Which return will the fleet trust?
options: Return C: measured aboard the ship

hints: A tester and a loop do the same thing every time. Which jack follows a person?
The fleet does not trust anything measured on the shore or in the booth.
Steve said which jack followed Shaw’s hand. Wen said which return is measured aboard the ship.
lines: c10_station.route.01
route.finding: steve|Elm follows Shaw’s hand, live, the way it did at the rig. Return C is a measurement signed aboard the Long Patience, the only kind the fleet trusts. Elm into Return C.

relay.title: Emergency radio
relay.goal: Find the operator who can actually see Sentinel Point.
relay.background: Saren’s crew have jammed every official channel. Frank, in wet pajamas and his old cardigan, is at the station’s emergency set. His Thursday club is on the air: Gull on the coast, Marsh out past Sentinel Point, and Cedar. Frank sent cue three yesterday and cue four today.
lead: c10_station.out.01
frank|The club sent signal three yesterday, without me. Today I’m sending signal four. Let’s see who keeps up.
steve|The official channel just sent back three. That’s yesterday’s cue.

lead.new: operator|Gull here. Cedar and Marsh both say four. Marsh says the wind just turned west out at the Point.

lead: frank|Ask them both about the wind again, Gull.

lead.new: operator|Marsh says it’s dropping now. Cedar said the same words as last time, exactly.

relay.prompt: Who should confirm tonight’s changing cues?

board.instruction: Read each reply and decide who is really watching the field.
evidence: Frank sent cue three yesterday and cue four today.
The jammed official line sent back cue three.
Cedar sent back cue four. Asked about the wind twice, Cedar gave the same words both times.
Marsh sent back cue four and gave a new wind reading each time he was asked.
Marsh lives out past Sentinel Point.

slots: Who has today’s cue but repeats old news?
Who can really see Sentinel Point?

board.wrong_text: Frank shakes his head. “Somebody on that list can’t see a thing, kiddo.”

hints: A reply with yesterday’s number is out of date.
Sending back the right number only proves someone heard Frank. Seeing the field means saying something new.
Which operator gave a fresh wind reading when Gull asked again?
lines: c10_station.relay.01
relay.finding: steve|The official line sent back yesterday’s cue. Cedar can repeat a cue but can’t see the field. Marsh, out past Sentinel Point, answered with a fresh wind reading. Marsh is our eyes, and Gull carries the cues down the coast.

recap: steve|KBWR is live again, and the tower that carried the ship’s signals for a year will carry ours: Elm into Return C.
steve|Dad’s club is relaying the cues. Marsh at Sentinel Point, Gull down the coast, and then anyone on Earth with a radio.
outro: frank|Every continent, kiddo. Hams never really switch off.

lines: frank|Has anybody got dry socks? I’ll trade a perfectly good vacuum tube.
steve|There’s a lost and found behind the coffee machine.
frank|Then I’m saving the world in somebody’s bowling socks.
frank|I wired half this booth, you know. Labeled every cable.
steve|Somebody took the labels off when the new owners came.
frank|Then I’ll put them back. Every single one. After breakfast.
stephen|Is there coffee? I remember liking coffee.
steve|You do. Black and very strong, two cups before breakfast.
stephen|Good. That one is still mine. I’m keeping it.
stephen|Do we both talk on air, or do we take turns?
steve|Take turns. People will think the radio is broken.
stephen|People already think that. I listened to your replacement for a week.
steve|Good morning, Rick. How are you feeling today?
autorick|I am excellent! It is currently yesterday!
steve|That sounds about right, buddy.
wen|When I was a girl, our village had one loudspeaker on a pole.
steve|What did the loudspeaker play all day?
wen|Weather, news and my aunt’s opinions. Mostly my aunt’s opinions.

c10_town.objective: Get the town, the lamps and the grid ready for one live show.
notes: Mrs. Penhallow’s reveal opens the scene and repeats the Archivist’s Veyr line word for word (p_veyr.out.01).
Ward’s line goes out on television (broadcast).

intro.new: steve|Mrs. Penhallow walked into the booth with her bait bucket. Nobody had told her where we were.

intro: agnes|Wind through the western towers. Last evening. Original take.
steve|Mrs. Penhallow, I have never heard you say anything that wasn’t about bait.

intro.text: I recorded it a long time ago, Steven. Before I had hands that smelled of herring.

intro: steve|You’re one of them. You’re the records officer Iris told me about.
agnes|Part of her. The part that stayed for the people.
agnes|Veyr was our home, Steven. Our sun failed. That is the last wind that ever blew through our city.

lights.title: Phone tree
lights.goal: Set up the porch lights so each street answers the one before it.
lights.background: Nora is running the town with her family’s phone tree. Two streets will flash their porch lights: Pier and Orchard. The Pier captain can see Orchard’s lights. Orchard faces the hills and can’t see Pier. Both streets have KBWR on. Mateo wants one phone kept free for the fire crew.
lead: nora|Two street captains, one spare phone and six thousand porch lights. Easy.
nora|Pier can see Orchard’s porch lights from the harbor. Orchard faces the hills, so they can’t see Pier at all.
nora|Both streets have the radio on. And Mateo wants one phone kept free for the fire crew.
lights.prompt: Which street starts, and what happens to the spare phone?
lights.instruction: The street that starts must hear Steve’s cue on the radio. The other street answers what it sees. The town still needs a free line for emergencies.

rows.label: What happens to the spare phone?
options: Keep it free for the fire crew
Join both captains in a show call

hints: Which street can see the other one’s lights?
The street that can see the other should answer it. So the other street has to start, from the radio.
Orchard can’t see Pier. And on a big night, the town still needs a line for the fire crew.
lines: c10_town.lights.01
lights.finding: steve|Nora set it up in ten minutes. Orchard starts on my cue, Pier answers what it sees, and the spare phone stays free for the fire crew.

console.title: Wen and Shaw
console.goal: Get Wen and Shaw onto one cue sheet.
console.background: Shaw’s lamps show when the harbor has answered. Wen’s grid crew can raise the load on the next beat. Nine years ago they faked rival tests. Tonight they share one console.
console.prompt: Shaw sees the harbor. Wen follows Shaw.
options: Put Shaw’s lamp mark on the cue sheet
hints: There is nothing to solve here.
There is nothing to solve here.
Put Shaw’s lamp mark on the cue sheet.
lines: c10_town.console.01
c10_town.console.02
c10_town.console.03
console.finding: steve|Shaw calls the lamps when she sees the harbor answer, and Wen raises the grid on Shaw’s mark. Nine years of rivalry, one cue sheet.

wind.title: The bait bucket
wind.goal: Give the fleet home as it was, then a voice answering now.
wind.background: Mrs. Penhallow’s spool holds the last wind on Veyr, nine hundred years old. The Choir can answer from aboard the ship, live.
lead: agnes|There is a pencil mark after the last gust. I made it myself.
steve|The fleet should hear home first. Then a voice answering them, live, that nobody recorded.
wind.prompt: The spool plays home as it was. The Choir must answer live, right after it. When does the Choir’s return open?
options: Restart the spool at the pencil mark
Open the Choir’s return after the last gust
Record the Choir onto the spool for every replay

wrong.0: Restarting it would just repeat a recording. That is the one thing the fleet must not hear.
wrong.2: Recorded, the Choir becomes one more replay. It has to answer live.

hints: Find the point where the old recording has finished.
The fleet must not hear anything repeat, and the Choir has to answer live.
A restart repeats, and a recording can’t answer. What is left when the last gust is over?
lines: c10_town.wind.01
wind.finding: steve|The Veyr wind plays through to Mrs. Penhallow’s pencil mark, after the last gust. Then the Choir’s return opens, live. Home as it was, then a voice answering them now.

recap: steve|Mrs. Penhallow is part of the ship’s record keeper, the part that stayed ashore with us. She brought me the last wind on Veyr in her bait bucket.
steve|Every porch light in Bellwether is waiting for my cue. Shaw has the lamps, Wen has the grid, and the Choir will answer live.

lines: nora|My mother has called forty people already. Thirty of them owe her money.
steve|Wait. People actually owe Carmen money?
nora|Tabs at the restaurant. She’s calling in every single one tonight.
nora|Yesterday I was asleep under the bay. Today I’m running a town.
steve|You were always running the town, Nor.
nora|True. But now people are actually listening to me.
nora|Iris called my brothers before I could. She knew every number by heart.
steve|She’s had your phone for five months.
nora|I want that phone back. And she rearranged all my apps.
carmen|I have called the bakery, the church and both bars. The bars were awake.
steve|Thank you, Carmen. I mean it.
carmen|Thank me by eating something. You haven’t eaten since Thursday. I can tell.
carmen|She argued with me twice tonight already. Twice, Steve!
steve|Is that a good thing?
carmen|It is the best night of my whole life.
agnes|You were a good student, Steven. Too loud. I liked that.
steve|You weren’t really my teacher, were you?
agnes|She was. I learned her very carefully. I only kept her chair warm.
steve|Why a bait stall, of all things?
agnes|Nobody buys bait, so nobody stays long. And I could watch the water all day.
ward|My staff wanted a long speech. I told them to listen to local radio.
steve|How is your wrist, Madam President?
ward|Bandaged, and still mine. Thank you for that.
wen|Nine years ago I would have unplugged her lamps.
shaw|You tried. And my fake fooled more generals than yours.
wen|It did not. My test fooled two admirals as well.
shaw|I brought the fog machine. Just in case.
steve|In case of what, exactly?
shaw|In case it needs to look impressive. It always needs to look impressive.

c10_live.objective: Run the live show. Each cue waits for you, so take your time.
notes: Saren’s threat goes out on air through the pier relay (delivery radio).
The Admiral line pays off the command crystal from the plot and Steve’s sandwich from Chapter 1.
Saren’s last line bridges to c10_report, where he is back aboard the ship.

intro.new: steve|I knocked over the microphone stand, caught it and kept going.

intro.text: Steve. Who’s... Frank. Dad. It’s on my hand.
It’s on mine too. Stay with me.

first.title: Cue one: a live reply
lead: nora|Orchard is listening for you, Steve. The pier is watching Orchard.
nora|Careful. Two Pier lamps are still on from the rehearsal. Don’t count those.
first.goal: Start the show with a reply nobody could have recorded.
first.background: The fleet’s instruments will be watching for a pattern that answers itself live. Nora’s phone tree is ready: Orchard hears KBWR, and Pier can see Orchard. Two Pier lamps are still glowing from the rehearsal.
first.prompt: Which street does Steve call, and what should release Shaw’s field lights?
first.instruction: Call the street that starts from the radio. Release Shaw’s field lights only when you see a new reply.

rows.label: When does Shaw switch on?
options: When the two old Pier lamps glow
At a new Pier flash after Orchard

hints: Remember Nora’s phone tree. Which street hears the radio, and which one watches?
A lamp that was already on tells Steve nothing. Shaw needs a reply.
Call the street that can only hear you. Then wait for the other street to answer what it saw.
lines: c10_live.first.01
c10_live.first.02
first.finding: steve|I called Orchard. When a fresh Pier flash answered Orchard’s change, I released Shaw’s lights. A reply, made live, that nobody could have recorded.

second.title: Cue two: the coast
lead: frank|I logged all three faders, kiddo. One of them only looks connected.
frank|With the coast plugged in, Reed and Bell both answered two beats late. With the coast unplugged, Reed went quiet.
frank|Bell kept answering anyway. So Bell is only an echo inside the building.
steve|The fourth signal goes out on beat forty. Shaw goes when the coast answers. Wen needs the next two beats.
wen|And my power crew needs everything back by the start of beat forty-five.
second.goal: Fit Shaw and Wen around the coast’s real reply.
second.background: Frank logged three faders on Steve’s beat clock. Test at 10, coast plugged in: Booth 10, Reed 12, Bell 12. Test at 20, coast unplugged: Booth 20, Reed silent, Bell 22. Cue four leaves at 40, and the power crew needs everything back at the start of beat 45.
second.prompt: Cue four goes out on beat 40. Which fader is the real coast, and which beats does Wen get?
second.instruction: The real coast goes quiet when the coast is unplugged. It answers two beats after a cue, and Shaw goes on that beat. Wen gets the next two beats, done before 45.

rows.label: Which fader is the real coast?

hints: Which fader stopped answering when Frank unplugged the coast?
The real coast answers two beats after a cue. Count on two beats from beat 40.
Shaw takes the beat the coast answers on. Wen takes the two beats right after that one.
lines: c10_live.second.01
c10_live.second.02
second.finding: steve|Reed went silent when the coast was unplugged, so Reed is the real coast return. Its reply landed at 42 for Shaw, and Wen took 43 and 44. Both grids answered, live.

third.title: Cue three: listen
lead: steve|Last cue. The wind on Veyr, and then the Choir. Nobody talks over them.
steve|Mrs. Penhallow marked the last gust at fifty. It keeps ringing until fifty-two.
wen|I confirm on beat fifty-one. Give me two beats to talk.
third.goal: Let the Choir speak with nothing in its way.
third.background: Last in the show comes the wind on Veyr, then the Choir, answering live. The fleet has not heard home in nine hundred years.
third.prompt: The last gust rings until beat 52. Wen talks on beats 51 and 52. The Choir should start on the first quiet beat. When does Steve open the Choir’s channel?

wrong.0: At 52 the gust is still ringing and Wen is still talking.
wrong.2: 54 is quiet, but it isn’t the first quiet beat. Count again from where Wen stops.

hints: When does the gust stop ringing, and when does Wen stop talking?
Both the gust and Wen are still going on beat 52.
Find the last beat that has any sound on it. The Choir starts on the beat after that.
lines: c10_live.third.01
c10_live.third.02

lines.new: steve|For the first time in nine hundred years, the fleet stopped to listen.

third.finding: steve|The wind on Veyr rang out through 52. At 53, with nobody else on the line, the Choir answered. Nothing repeated, because nothing was recorded.

recap: steve|Porch lights, field lamps, two national grids, a planet’s worth of radios and three hundred and twelve human voices. None of it recorded. All of it answering.
steve|To the Vigil’s instruments, Earth had just tested an engine that could reach the fleet in an afternoon.

outro.new: saren|Mr. Mercer. Turn it off, or I will come up that tower and finish your scan on air.

outro: steve|You’re on air now, Prefect. Your whole fleet is listening. Say that again.

outro.new: steve|The town stood on the pier in his way. June. The Reyes brothers. Carmen with a ladle. Pell with Biscuit. Stephen. And two hundred copies who had decided where they lived.

outro: carmen|He’s sitting down. Mateo is sitting on him.

outro.text: And Admiral has stolen his command crystal. He thinks it’s a sandwich.

outro: saren|Take me back to the ship. I will not sign anything.
c10_live.next: The ship’s antenna room and the open channel (c10_report).

c10_report.objective: Decide what the fleet will hear.
changes: missing (the Archivist’s motive for her notebook lie)
notes: The Archivist’s new line explains Interlude 1: she wrote ‘Engine details in subject’s notebook’ so Saren would keep searching instead of telling the fleet there was nothing on Earth to fear.
AutoRick’s last line on air is a forecast for yesterday (plot).

context.new: steve|Mrs. Penhallow took the microphone out of my hand. Then she argued with herself, on the air, while the whole planet listened.

intro: archivist|For a year I told you the engine was in a notebook, Saren. So you would keep looking, instead of telling the fleet there was nothing here to fear.

echo.title: The open channel
echo.goal: Find a witness to life on shore.
echo.background: A report to the fleet needs the word of the Prefect or the Archivist. Saren refuses. To confirm it, the Archivist must break every law she has kept for nine hundred years, and she wants a witness first. Her shore echo has sold bait on the pier for three years. Last winter, when the boats came in empty, she let the fishermen pay in spring. The real Agnes slept in row three the whole time.
lead: agnes|Last winter the boats came in empty. I let every one of them pay me in spring.
echo.prompt: The Archivist wants a witness who has lived on shore with these people. Who can speak for life in Bellwether?
options: The Archivist, reading her departure register
Her shore echo, with last winter’s credit ledger
Mrs. Penhallow, still waking up in row three

wrong.0: The register is nine hundred years old. It knows nothing about Bellwether.
wrong.2: The real Agnes has been asleep in row three for three years. She has never met these customers.

hints: Who has actually lived on shore?
The register is nine hundred years old, and the real Agnes has been asleep for three years.
A witness to life on shore has to have lived it, last winter, behind the bait counter.
lines: c10_report.echo.01
c10_report.echo.02
echo.finding: archivist|My echo stood behind the bait counter last winter and let the boats pay in spring. I remember the wind. She remembers the people. I will let her win.

survey.title: The sealed survey
survey.goal: Find the fleet somewhere else to live.
survey.background: Nine nights ago, on the last ninth night, the Archivist filed the Prefect’s sealed entry unread. Tonight the Choir has opened every door and every seal on the ship.
lead: archivist|There is a sealed survey in the Prefect’s file. He told us every world was taken.
archivist|Three slips. Reef Six has water and air, and a beacon there answers every call.
archivist|Sound Four has air, but no water at all. Reach Two has water and air, and it was visited three times.
survey.prompt: Which world should the fleet be told about, and what shows the ground is empty?
survey.instruction: The fleet needs a world with water, air and nobody living there yet. A beacon that answers means someone already lives there.

rows.label: Which world should the fleet hear about?
What shows the ground is empty?

hints: The fleet needs water, air and room to settle.
A beacon that answers every call means somebody already lives there. A world with no water can’t take the fleet.
One world was checked on three separate visits. What did those visits find?
lines: c10_report.survey.01
c10_report.survey.02
survey.finding: archivist|Reach 2: water, air and three separate surveys of empty ground. The Prefect found a home for the fleet and sealed it, because a home would have ended his mission.

report.title: Fleet transmission
report.goal: Build a report the fleet will believe.
report.background: The fleet acts only on a report signed aboard its own ship. The Archivist wants it to carry three things: proof of danger, a place to go, and an introduction.
report.prompt: Which evidence goes with each part of the report?

board.instruction: Attach one piece of evidence to each part of the report.
evidence: The fleet only trusts measurements taken aboard the Long Patience.
The ship’s own instrument measured the live show from Earth.
The Reach 2 survey shows a world with water, air and empty ground.
The Choir’s ledger holds three hundred and twelve human lives.
board.wrong_text: The Archivist pauses. The fleet would not accept that attachment for that claim.

hints: The fleet trusts its own ship’s instruments more than anything else.
The survey is about a place. The ledger is about people.
Danger needs a measurement the fleet trusts. A home needs ground surveyed empty. What is left is an introduction.
lines: c10_report.report.01
c10_report.report.02
c10_report.report.03
report.finding: archivist|The danger, measured aboard our own ship. A home, surveyed empty three times. And three hundred and twelve people worth meeting. I have confirmed the report.

recap: archivist|The report is confirmed. The fleet will measure an engine that does not exist, meet three hundred and twelve people, and learn of a home it was never told about.
archivist|I did not reconcile Saren. He will have to live with being wrong. So will I.

outro.new: autorick|And now, the forecast for yesterday: sunny, with a chance of spaceships!
steve|The Vigil turned, and the fleet turned with it. At sunrise the Long Patience rose out of the bay, with Wick aboard. The whole coast watched it go. Somebody on the pier started to clap.

notes: All three tasks stay non-graded beats.

neighbors.goal: Say good morning to the town.
neighbors.background: More than two hundred copies chose to stay. Bellwether has a lot of new neighbors with familiar faces.
neighbors.finding: steve|Two fathers for Lyle’s boys, a new mail carrier for Biscuit, and a green croissant.

bait.goal: Visit the bait shop and the ferry.
bait.background: Two Mrs. Penhallows now share one counter. At the ferry, Adrian Rook is saying goodbye to the man who wore his face.
bait.finding: steve|Two Mrs. Penhallows, one counter, and people are finally buying bait. One Adrian Rook stays. The other one is leaving town, to find out who he is.

coffee.background: There is a new note on the kitchen table every morning now.
coffee.finding: steve|Mom and Dad are home. There’s a note on the table. And Nora is waiting at the door.

recap: steve|Bellwether kept its new neighbors. And on every ninth night now, the town puts lanterns on the water.

lines: nora|I go back to the aquarium on Monday. The otter pups won’t remember me.
steve|They’ll remember you. You’re the one who argues with the vet.
nora|Everybody argues with the vet. I just win.
nora|Somebody rearranged our kitchen. Everything is in alphabetical order.
steve|That was Iris. She thought it looked tidy.
nora|The forks are under F. I’m leaving them there. It makes me laugh every morning.
nora|Admiral came to my whistle this morning. Straight out of the water.
steve|Your second note went up again. I heard it from the pier.
nora|It always went up, Steve. Somebody else was whistling it wrong.
iris|I chose this face myself. It’s strange to be surprised by a mirror.
steve|It suits you. It really does.
iris|Nora says the nose is too serious. I think that means she likes it.
iris|Carmen invited me to dinner on Sunday. Is that a trap?
steve|With Carmen, dinner and a trap can be the same thing.
iris|Then I’ll bring bread. Nora says bread is always safe.
carmen|Six o’clock, Steve. Both of you. All of you.
steve|You mean Iris is invited too?
carmen|Iris too. She sat at my table for five months. Now she can help with the dishes.
carmen|I kept your plate warm every Sunday. This Monday I am not throwing it out.
steve|You never had to keep it, Carmen.
carmen|I know. That is why I did.
lyle|Ben has the school play tonight. He wants both of us in the front row.
steve|Two Lyle Boones in one front row.
lyle|The other one learned the lines with him. I’m still learning mine.
lyle_copy|I still go to every game. Now we take turns driving.
lyle|He’s better at the snacks. I’m better at yelling at the umpire.
lyle_copy|We’re working on that. Both of us.
pell|Biscuit knows every porch on the route. I am still learning the gates.
dale|The blue gate on Harbor Street sticks. Kick it low.
pell|Kick it low. I have written that down.
dale|First free morning in thirty years. No mailbag, and no frozen bed.
steve|What are you going to do instead, Dale?
dale|Sleep in a real bed. A warm one. Then go fishing.
gus|Try it, Steve. It’s green, but it’s honest.
steve|Gus, this is actually really good.
gus|Don’t tell anyone. I have a reputation for plain bread.
agnes_original|She charges ten cents less than me for worms. On purpose.
agnes|Somebody kept this stall open for three years, Agnes.
agnes_original|And in three years, nobody bought a single worm.
agnes|The ship left without me, Steven. I asked it to.
steve|Won’t you miss the wind back home?
agnes|I have the wind on a spool. I would miss the people more.
rook|I have a lot of reports to write. Nobody is going to believe them.
steve|Write them anyway, Adrian. Every word.
rook|That’s what June said. Word for word.
rook_copy|I’m leaving town today. I want to find out who I am when nobody is watching.
steve|Good luck out there. I mean it.
rook_copy|Tell June I’m sorry about the voicemail.
helen|Your father leaves me a note every morning now. Today’s note says the kettle is labeled.
steve|Is the kettle actually labeled now?
helen|Kettle. In capital letters. I married a very thorough man.
helen|I keep hearing Wick’s phrase when I do the dishes.

answer.prompt: Three in the morning. A real signal from deep space: two joined tones, the second climbing, a gap, then one long tone lower than both. Helen has three pages open.
options: Page 12: two joined strokes rising, a gap, one long low stroke
Page 4: one long stroke, a gap, two joined strokes falling

wrong.0: Three separate strokes. Nothing is joined, and nothing climbs.
wrong.2: That shape starts with the long stroke and falls. This signal climbs first.

hints: Follow the shape: joined, climbing, a gap, then low.

panels: Before the ship left, the Choir gave the copies one last gift. They don’t need the ninth night anymore.
More than two hundred of them stayed. Bellwether has a lot of new neighbors with familiar faces.
Iris chose a face of her own. People still say hello to the wrong Steve sometimes. We both say hello back.
Mom and Dad came home. Dad is back on the radio every Thursday.
Dad labels everything now. The paint, the radios, me.
I don’t play the old voicemail anymore.
The ring isn’t in the sock drawer anymore. Ask Nora where it is.
Nora argues with me again. About everything. I missed it more than I can say.
KBWR has live hosts again. Two of them.
Stephen and I still argue about which one of us is the upgrade.
One year after the ninth night, a package arrived at the station.
